title: How Rainbows Form
passages: Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of many colors traveling together. When the sun shines from behind you and rain is falling in front of you, the light meets millions of tiny raindrops. As light enters a drop, it slows down and bends. This bending is called REFRACTION. Each color bends by a slightly different amount, so the colors begin to spread apart, like runners fanning out on a track.

Inside the drop, the light bounces off the curved back wall, a step called REFLECTION. Then it bends again as it leaves, spreading the colors even farther. Red shows on the outer edge of the bow and violet on the inner edge, with orange, yellow, green and blue between them. This band of colors is called a SPECTRUM. Every person sees their own rainbow, made by a different set of drops. People in many cultures have told stories about rainbows, imagining them as bridges, serpents or messages from the sky, which shows how this bright arc has filled people everywhere with wonder.
